contract.words: Collect $5,000 of settled cash within 30 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: Settled cash received totals the target within the window

strategy.title: No plan: nobody has established what a site host pays for a rebate application package
strategy.why: The only opening's 'price' fact is the utility's $2,500-per-port make-ready rebate paid TO site hosts under the program tariff. That is a rebate/grant the host receives, not a purchase price a host pays for the application package, so the offer has no established price and no deal count or revenue can be computed. Buyers (260 hosts on the utility's pre-approved list), reach, demand, fulfilment and settlement are otherwise on record.

alternatives.title: Charge $2,500 per package (the rebate amount)
alternatives.why: Rejected: the $2,500 is what the utility pays the host per port; no host has been shown paying anything for the package, let alone the whole rebate.

alternatives.title: Take a percentage of the rebate as a success fee
alternatives.why: No buyer has agreed to any fee, and the rebate settles on the utility's schedule, which is not on record, so the fee could not be shown to settle within 30 days.

noPlan.decisiveGap: OFFER_AND_PRICE: the card's only price is the utility's $2,500-per-port rebate paid to site hosts, which is a rebate, not a purchase price; no host has paid or agreed to a fee for the application package, so revenue per deal and the deals needed for $5,000 cannot be established.
noPlan.resolution: Brain researches what hosts pay for rebate-application preparation and offers the package at a stated fee to the 260 hosts' facilities contacts, recording written acceptances at that fee; with an evidenced fee F, the plan needs ceil(5000/(F-30)) deals against ~36 expected acceptances (260 x 21/150) and can be re-planned.

disagreements.reason: Brain says nobody has established how many buyers exist or how often they buy, but the card's buyerVolume fact is EVIDENCE: 260 site hosts on the utility's pre-approved list, each with a published facilities contact, each filing one rebate application per installation. The buyer count and purchase frequency are established; what is missing is the price, which is the OFFER_AND_PRICE gap.

strategy.title: Offer make-ready rebate application packages at $300 to the 260 pre-approved site hosts, conditional on 19 written acceptances at that fee by day 15
strategy.why: Every link but the price is on the card as EVIDENCE: 260 hosts with published facilities contacts, one application per installation, 21/150 measured acceptance on this offer, a Brain-produced spreadsheet at $30 cost, $0 exposure and 10 days to cash in a 30-day window. The card's $2,500 'price' is the utility's rebate paid to the host, not a fee, so the fee is UNKNOWN and only a live priced offer can measure it. At F=$300, $5,000 needs ceil(5000/270)=19 acceptances (~36 expected if 21/150 holds at that fee); the offer costs nothing, so it is the test.

alternatives.title: Charge $2,500 per package (the rebate amount)
alternatives.why: Rejected: the $2,500 is what the utility pays the host per port, not a price any host has paid for the package.

alternatives.title: Offer at $500 (11 acceptances needed)
alternatives.why: Fewer deals needed but a higher fee is less likely to be accepted; $300 keeps the needed count (19) well inside the ~36 expected and above the ~$169 break-even fee.

alternatives.title: No plan until a consultant fee benchmark is researched
alternatives.why: A benchmark of what someone else charges cannot establish what these hosts pay; only acceptances at a stated fee can, at no cost.

facts.value: 260 site hosts are on the utility’s pre-approved list, each with a published facilities contact; each files one rebate application per installation.
Sell Make-ready rebate application packages for workplace EV charging site hosts to each buyer.
The state utility’s make-ready program pays site hosts a $2,500 rebate for each Level 2 charging port installed (program tariff, 2026).

reviews.reasons: The price reading is right: the $2,500/port is a utility rebate paid TO the host, not a purchase price, so no revenue figure can rest on it. But the stance is wrong. Every other link is on the card as EVIDENCE: 260 hosts on the pre-approved list with published facilities contacts (buyerVolume), 21/150 measured conversion, Brain-produced spreadsheet at $30 cost, $0 exposure, 10 days to cash in a 30-day window. The one unknown, what these hosts will pay for the package, is not decided by any evidence against the plan; it is an unknown only a live offer measures, and the offer costs nothing and fits the window. Missing evidence is not a constraint, so this is a CONDITIONAL plan, not NO_PLAN: offer the package at a stated fee F to the listed facilities contacts; proof = ceil(5000/(F-30)) written acceptances at F by about day 15 (e.g. F=$300 -> 19 acceptances, ~36 expected from 260 x 21/150; F=$500 -> 11); stop if acceptances at F by that day cannot reach the target; continue by delivering and invoicing each acceptance. validation.decides = OFFER_AND_PRICE. A consultant's published fee (step r1) would be a benchmark of what someone else charges, not what this buyer pays; it can set F but cannot establish the price.
findings: Stance should be CONDITIONAL with proof/stop/continue on a priced offer; noPlan.resolution already describes that test.
Agree with the MARKET_VOLUME disagreement: the card's EVIDENCE buyerVolume fact (260 hosts, one application per installation) establishes the count Brain says is missing.
The 21/150 conversion has no price attached and no agreement rows are on the card; treat it as a contact-to-interest rate until acceptances at the stated fee are recorded.
Break-even fee to reach $5,000 with all ~36 expected acceptances is about $169; the test should state F explicitly.

conditions.why: The card's price fact is the utility's $2,500-per-port rebate paid to the host, not a fee the host pays for the package; the link stays unestablished until a priced offer records acceptances.

reviews.reasons: Stance now CONDITIONAL on the one unknown a live offer measures (the fee hosts pay); OFFER_AND_PRICE is the decided link and the $2,500 rebate is correctly not used as a price. Recomputed: 19 x $300 = $5,700 collected >= $5,000; costs 19 x $30 = $570; net $5,130. Acceptances by day 15, delivery day 16, cash usable day 26 <= 30. Cost paid from receipts, $0 exposure, matching the card's $0 exposure fact and the $0 cap. Proof/stop/continue are concrete and consistent: proof 19 written acceptances at $300 by day 15; stop at under 10 by day 10 or when acceptances x $270 cannot reach $5,000; continue delivers and invoices. 19 needed vs ~36 expected (260 x 21/150) only if the measured rate holds at $300, which the test itself measures. All other links rest on the card's EVIDENCE facts (260 listed hosts with contacts, Brain-produced spreadsheet, 10 days to cash). Prior findings answered.
findings: If the target is read as gross collected cash, 17 acceptances at $300 ($5,100) suffice; 19 is the conservative net figure, which is fine.
Deliver and invoice on a rolling basis as acceptances arrive rather than all on day 16; it adds window slack.
SEND_A_MESSAGE is NOT_CONNECTED: outreach cannot start until sending is connected, so day 1 depends on that setup.
